Highlight Clip: Jeff Yan: TradFi's Speed Arms Race Is Zero-Sum — and Even Negative-Sum Jeff Yan: TradFi's Speed Arms Race Is Zero-Sum — and Even Negative-Sum Hyperliquid Labs co-founder Jeff Yan said at DAS Asia 2026 on October 7 that he does not view Hyperliquid’s priority fee mechanism as “bribery.” Its purpose, he said, is to reduce advantages from low-latency infrastructure and make genuine trading alpha more important. Yan argued that the latency race in traditional finance — involving microwave towers and transatlantic fiber cables — is fundamentally zero-sum, and sometimes even negative-sum, because it creates little meaningful value. Hyperliquid aims to use priority fees to internalize these negative externalities, allowing traders to compete more fairly without spending heavily on low-latency infrastructure. — link

Highlight Clip: Vitalik Buterin: Without AI, Ethereum's Lean Roadmap Might Have to Wait Until 2040 Vitalik Buterin: Without AI, Ethereum's Lean Roadmap Might Have to Wait Until 2040 Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said in an October 9 interview with Balaji Srinivasan at the Network State Conference 2026 that AI has become an important factor in advancing the Lean Ethereum roadmap. Buterin said that given the roadmap's current goals and level of ambition, without AI, the work might have taken until 2040 or even 2050 to complete. He added that AI is now contributing to a significant amount of research and coding, substantially accelerating progress on the roadmap. — link

Fake Ledger Phishing Site Tops Google Search Results with Over 1M Monthly Visits According to Bitcoin News, amid ongoing investigations into an estimated $86 million in wallet thefts linked to Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, security researcher Cyber Scrilla discovered a fraudulent Ledger phishing website and application appearing at the top of Google Search, designed to trick users into submitting their 24-word recovery phrases. Google reportedly displays more than 1 million visits over the past 30 days. The alert follows a September investigation by cybersecurity firm Zscaler, which uncovered malicious Google ads impersonating Ledger and redirecting users to fake wallet-verification pages. — link

Highlight Clip: Star Xu: How Did USDe Leverage Loops Trigger the "1010" Crash? Star Xu: How Did USDe Leverage Loops Trigger the "1010" Crash? OKX founder and CEO Star Xu questioned Binance's promotion of USDe as a stablecoin on the New Era Finance Podcast. He argued that USDe, issued by Ethena, is effectively a "tokenized hedge fund" and that a delta-neutral strategy does not imply zero or low risk. He further noted that Binance allowed users to borrow USDT against USDe, convert it into more USDe, and repeat the loop to increase yields, amplifying leverage and risk exposure along the way. In his view, this setup was a major cause of the cascading liquidations during the "1010" crash and represented a serious risk-control failure. — link
